newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seesaw to close moderately lower.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seesaw to close moderately lower.

text.p: Argentine stocks moved erratically with a negative bias Tuesday but trimmed losses at the close, dealers said.

"The session was very choppy, and while at the opening stocks tried to extend the rally of the previous two sessions they pulled back on speculative selling," said trader Miguel Daneri of Boston Securities. "I'd say the market took a break and the heavy volume denotes its underlying strength."
The blue-chip MerVal index, which surged 4.3 percent between Friday and Monday on strong foreign bidding, shed 0.9 percent to 757.67.
"Those who sold have a hard time getting back into the market with cheaper prices, so stocks will probably revert back to gains tomorrow," said Daneri.
Floor volume remained uncharacteristically heavy at 42.5 million pesos against 41.7 million Monday, while over-the-counter volume swelled to 168.1 million pesos from 93 million Monday.
Traders noted optimism on the bolsa mirrored a winning streak in the other Latin American markets.
"Brazil and Chile were sharply up today while on the bolsa there was some normal profit-taking," another trader said.
The broad market index eased 0.4 percent, with losers outpacing winners 36 to 24 and 19 issues closing flat.
Heaviest MerVal losers were steelmaker Acindar, construction stock Polledo and pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which slid 3.4 percent, 2.6 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively.

Best main-tier performers were power distributor Central Costanera, which jumped 2.9 percent, holding company Comercial del Plata, up 1.3 percent, and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, up 0.5 percent.
